generations.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: transparent sprite sheet for one original stationary Tantalus Choir organism, four visual functions.

Primary request: Design one ORIGINAL Tantalus organism for the existing stationary Choir target role. Its proposed anatomy is an original project choice, not a documented franchise caste. Make one 2 by 2 sheet of the exact same organism in four states, in reading order: presence A, presence B, reaction after being hit, neutralized. Request 2048 by 2048 pixels; actual dimensions will be measured afterward.

Reference roles, if attached:
Image 1 is the existing red adult modular body sheet: use only the rendering finish, ribbed chitin materials and restrained ivory highlights. Do not copy its adult body, head, crown, limbs or tail.
Image 2 is the native scene: use only its dark warm environment as a legibility context. Do not draw any of the environment, characters, pink placeholder shapes, UI, lettering, platform, props or effects.
Neither reference establishes Choir anatomy. The silhouette described below is the target.

Subject and silhouette: A low fixed holdfast with two broad, fused, non-articulated support lobes. From that base rises a narrow living central stem that branches into two thick asymmetrical curved ribbed blades, forming an OPEN COSTAL ARCH. Leave an obvious open notch at the top and a slight constriction below the arch. A vertically stretched matte wine/mauve membrane hangs in the lower portion between the blades; it does not close the upper notch. The outer contour must remain forked and open, never a sealed oval. The membrane and several broad rib ridges, not a face, are the visual focus. This is living tissue and chitin, with naturally integrated seams and no manufactured joints. No head, mouth, eyes, arms, hands, walking legs, wings or long tail. No egg shell, four opening egg petals, larvae, nest, flower, instrument, pylon or machine. The stable supports do not lift or slide.

View and rendering: One consistent shallow three-quarter view turned slightly toward screen right, suitable for a side-view 2D game. Same camera, perspective, lighting direction, structural proportions and drawing scale in every cell. Detailed game-creature illustration with clear large forms and restrained fine texture. At a living height of 90 game pixels the open fork, membrane, support and reaction must still read. Prefer six to eight broad primary ribs to a dense mesh of tiny filaments.

Materials and colors: Near-black wine chitin, muted red-brown raised plates, opaque dusty mauve/burgundy membrane, sparse warm ivory-grey ridges. Use ordinary reflected light to separate the principal ridges and the membrane from a dark brown scene. These lighter ridges must remain present in the neutralized state; do not pre-fade that cell. No neon edge, aura, glow, haze, smoke, bloom, colored spill or transparent fog outside the body.

Four cells:
TOP LEFT, presence A: erect open arch, membrane gently tensioned, base firmly supported.
TOP RIGHT, presence B: the same supports and rigid outer arch, only a very slight change in membrane tension and nearby soft tissue. It must not become taller than presence A or suggest a step, attack, sonic blast or new power.
BOTTOM LEFT, reaction: a compact contraction after receiving a hit. The upper blades bend inward and slightly down around the membrane; the same body, same support base, no wound effects or attacking pose. Make the retraction distinguishable at 90 pixels without any change of scale.
BOTTOM RIGHT, neutralized: the same arch has folded down into two clearly recognizable ribbed blades resting against the original base. The membrane is slack. The intact body is roughly half its living height because it is folded, not shrunk. Keep the structural junction and support base at the same horizontal anchor and ground line. It is inert with no fragments, explosion, gore, liquid, projectile or impact effect. Render the source at normal full opacity; the game applies its own fading.

Composition and invariants: Four equal square cells in a clean 2 by 2 layout with no drawn grid. Same anatomical scale everywhere, never fit each pose independently to its cell. In each cell use a common structural base anchor near horizontal50percent and vertical86percent. Presence A is about70percent of the cell height; presence B must stay at or below that height. Leave generous transparent margins around every blade and support, including the lower margin. Living width is about48percent of a cell; a folded body may widen slightly while preserving the same scale. Every body is complete. No part crosses a cell boundary. No additional organisms or detached pieces.

Transparency: Real transparent RGBA background. Outside the actual silhouettes must be fully transparent except narrow edge antialiasing. Internal open spaces must also be genuinely transparent. No painted checkerboard, studio backdrop, floor plane, cast shadow or environmental reflection. No text, numbers, names, labels, borders or watermark.
